issues.title: [Docs][personal-assistant]: README badge and OpenAPI metadata say MIT, LICENSE and pyproject say Apache-2.0
issues.text:
### Affected Component
`statewave-personal-assistant` — `README.md`, `app/main.py`

### Bug Description
The repo states two different licenses:

| Where | Says |
|---|---|
| `LICENSE` | Apache License 2.0 |
| `pyproject.toml` | `license = { text = "Apache-2.0" }` + Apache classifier |
| `README.md:8` | badge **"License: MIT"** linking to `LICENSE` |
| `app/main.py:83` | `license_info={"name": "MIT"}` — shown in the OpenAPI `/docs` page |

So the README badge and the API docs say MIT, while the actual license file says Apache 2.0.

### Expected Behavior
Everything says Apache-2.0, matching `LICENSE`.

### Suggested fix
- `README.md:8`: change the badge to `license-Apache--2.0-blue`.
- `app/main.py:83`: `license_info={"name": "Apache-2.0", "url": "https://www.apache.org/licenses/LICENSE-2.0"}`.

### Environment
`main` @ `e89f33b`.

### Severity
Low — but license metadata is something people check before adopting code.

issues.title: Documentation Suggestion: Exposing the API Port
issues.text:
I was looking for monitoring solution with an API I could access and use in my own project's. Peekaping is great for this purpose but the only thing is the documentation currently doesn't mention how to expose the API anywhere when running it in a Docker container. Took me awhile to figure it out but it was so easy and I think it should definitely be part of the documentation. If you want to expose the API just add port 8034 to the docker container its ports and after that the entire API is available at localhost:8034/api/v1/ and the docs are viewable at localhost:8034/swagger/index.html.

Docker Command: 
`docker run -d --restart=always \
  -p 8383:8383 \
  -p 8034:8034 \
  -e DB_NAME=/app/data/peekaping.db \
  -v $(pwd)/.data/sqlite:/app/data \
  --name peekaping \
  0xfurai/peekaping-bundle-sqlite:latest`

At first I was completely confused and thought I had to run a dev server for this. But if you just want to access the API without changing anything to Peekaping itself exposing the port is all you have to do really. Here an example of an ESP32 based display fetching the latest heartbeat of a monitor(using one monitor for all 8 services as a proof of concept): 

![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/c4e82fce-adb9-4f99-aecf-ad3f131138e8)

issues.title: [Bug] The artifact preview endpoint silently clamps `?maxRows=` to 100 and caps the column set at 1,001, so an outside API caller gets less than it asked for
issues.text:
## What happens

`GET` artifact version preview (`services/api/src/artifact-dashboard.ts`, `buildArtifactVersionPreview` → `parseDelimitedTable` / `recordArrayTable`) now bounds its payload with two server-side constants:

- `const maxRows = Math.min(MAX_PREVIEW_ROWS, parsePositiveInt(maxRowsParam, DEFAULT_MAX_ROWS));` — `MAX_PREVIEW_ROWS = DEFAULT_MAX_ROWS = 100` (`artifact-dashboard.ts:719` at `0477d328`)
- `const width = Math.min(totalColumns, MAX_PREVIEW_COLUMNS);` — `MAX_PREVIEW_COLUMNS = 1_001` (`artifact-dashboard.ts:398`)

A caller that asks for more gets less, with no error: the response just carries `truncated` and `clippedColumns`/`clippedCells`.

## Measured at `0477d328`

- 1,500-column CSV → `columns 1001`, `clippedColumns {shown 1001, total 1500}`, `clippedCells 499` (named columns past 1,001 are dropped).
- 401-row CSV at `?maxRows=400` → `rows 100`, `totalRows 400`, `truncated true`.
- 500-record JSON at `?maxRows=400` → the same 100 rows (the clamp applies to the record-array path too).

## Why it matters

The bundled web client never sends `maxRows` (`apps/web/src/api/artifacts.ts:201` forwards an optional value only, and `apps/desktop` reads local CSV), so there is no in-repo regression — but for any other API caller this is a silent contract change: asking for 400 rows returns 100, and a legitimately wide table loses named columns. `#829` asked for a preview that keeps every row as wide as the columns it advertises; the bound is what makes the payload fin

issues.title: SQL on an edge: `out` and `in` silently return null (the endpoints are `@out` / `@in`); a docs line or an error would help
issues.text:
On an edge, SQL reads the endpoints as `@out` and `@in` (the docs use them throughout, e.g. `CREATE INDEX ... (@out, @in)` and `WHERE @out = #12:0`), and `outV()` / `inV()` work too. Plain `out` and `in` are not fields of an edge, but reading them is not an error: they return null, and so does every path through them. A query written the OrientDB way, or by someone who guesses the field name, silently returns nulls instead of failing.

**Reproducer** (ArcadeDB 26.10.2 through the Python bindings `arcadedb-embedded` 26.10.2.post1; the statements are plain SQL, so any client shows the same):

```python
import arcadedb_embedded as arcadedb
with arcadedb.create_database("./t") as db:
    db.command("sql", "CREATE VERTEX TYPE A"); db.command("sql", "CREATE VERTEX TYPE B"); db.command("sql", "CREATE EDGE TYPE E")
    with db.transaction():
        db.command("sql", "INSERT INTO A SET id = 1"); db.command("sql", "INSERT INTO B SET name = 'x'")
        db.command("sql", "CREATE EDGE E FROM (SELECT FROM A) TO (SELECT FROM B) SET qty = 7")
    for q in ("SELECT out.id FROM E", "SELECT in.name FROM E", "SELECT out FROM E", "SELECT @out.id FROM E", "SELECT outV().id FROM E"):
        print(q, [r.to_dict() for r in db.query("sql", q)])
```

| Query | Result |
|---|---|
| `SELECT out.id FROM E` | `[{'out.id': None}]` |
| `SELECT in.name FROM E` | `[{'in.name': None}]` |
| `SELECT out FROM E` | `[{'out': None}]` |
| `SELECT @out.id FROM E` | `[{'@out.id': 1}]` |
| `SELECT outV().id FROM E`

issues.title: OrcaRouter provider support for Bernstein (as an OpenAI-compatible endpoint)
issues.text:
### Problem

Bernstein tackles a problem few orchestrators address head-on: coordination that stays fully deterministic while the models doing the work remain interchangeable. Policy-as-code plus a plain-Python scheduler makes a run replay to the same task graph, and signed receipts let an operator verify a run offline from the artifacts alone — the README's origin story of parallel coding agents producing nondeterministic merges is the exact failure mode it removes.

That same operator is why I think Bernstein gains from more provider choice. `provider_availability` already gives each role an ordered fallback chain of `(adapter, model)` pairs, health-probed before dispatch and recorded as a routing receipt. The missing piece is more certified endpoints to place in that chain.

### Proposed solution

Add OrcaRouter as an **optional** provider that operators can point a Bernstein adapter at. It would not replace or alter any existing provider, adapter behaviour, or scope boundary. Concretely:

- Document pointing an adapter at OrcaRouter's OpenAI-compatible endpoint in `bernstein.yaml`, the token supplied through an env-var name (as with `api_key_env`) rather than an inline secret, mirroring the `clm`/Ollama lanes.
- Let operators qualify it with tooling Bernstein already ships for any OpenAI-compatible server — `bernstein endpoints certify` / `bernstein doctor --endpoint` — so an OrcaRouter entry reaches a `provider_availability` chain only after passing the conformance probe

issues.title: shared/dlp: exported pattern-lookup API has no doc comments
issues.text:
None of the exported functions in packages/shared/dlp.go carry a doc comment. DLPPatternCount, DLPPatternNames, DLPPatternAt, DLPPatternIndex, DLPHitRank, DLPScan, DLPScanViews, and GlobToRegexp are the public surface other packages use to drive DLP scanning, but their parameters and return semantics are only discoverable by reading the body. For example DLPHitRank's returned int is a priority rank used to pick the "earliest" pattern match, and GlobToRegexp only treats runs of "*" as a wildcard and quotes everything else literally, and neither fact is stated anywhere near the function signature.

Add a short doc comment above each exported function in dlp.go stating what it does, what its parameters mean, and what its return value represents, so a new contributor can use the API without tracing through the implementation.

Create `docs/API.md` covering every public method on `HolographicMemorySystem`:

For each method, include:
- Signature (from `index.d.ts`)
- One-sentence description
- A 3-5 line usage example
- Return type explanation

| Group | Methods |
|-------|---------|
| Core | `memorizeText`, `memorizeTextBuffer`, `memorizeVector`, `memorizeScalar`, `memorizeBatch`, `memorizeFile` |

issues.title: API docs: OpenAPI paths cannot be resolved against the declared server (43 of 239 private operations 404)
issues.text:
## Summary

The generated OpenAPI specs declare a single server (`{scheme}://{host}/api`), but the `paths` are written in two different conventions depending on which route tree they came from. As a result, a client that resolves a path against the declared server — which is what OpenAPI tooling does by definition — builds a 404 URL for **43 of the 239 private operations (18%)**.

Found while building an Expo/React Native client against the published spec. The specs are genuinely useful and most of the surface is correct; this is about the subset that can't be resolved mechanically.

## Why it happens

`generate.php` scans five route trees into one document:

```
api/routes/  admin/routes/api/  finance/routes/api/  kiosk/routes/api/  plugins/routes/api/
```

Routes under `api/routes/` are mounted at `/api`, so their docblock paths are written *relative* to that mount and match `servers`. The module trees mount under their own prefix (`/admin`, `/finance`, `/kiosk`, `/plugins`) and write paths *absolute from the site root*. One `servers` entry can't describe both.

## 1. Module paths are root-absolute (28 operations)

| `/admin/api/import/csv/families` | `/admin/api/import/csv/families` | `/api/admin/api/import/csv/families` ❌ |
| `/kiosk/api/devices` | `/kiosk/api/devices` | `/api/kiosk/api/devices` ❌ |
| `/plugins/api/plugins` | `/plug

issues.title: Epic: Contract-first public API - single-source endpoints + doc consolidation
issues.text:
## Problem

Our API documentation and contracts are fragmented and drift-prone:

- The public **OpenAPI spec** (`/api/v1/openapi.json`, Scalar UI at `/api/v1/docs`) is generated from runtime Zod and drift-gated in CI, but covers only **2 operations**.
- A **~1,400-line hand-written Markdown reference** (`apps/client/app/components/admin/content/apiReferenceContent.ts`, rendered in the admin API Reference tab) documents the whole surface but is **unverified** and silently drifts from the code.
- Across ~718 route files, the request contract lives **inline in the handler** in ~227 of them; only ~26 import a shared schema. The contract is trapped where docs, SDKs, and types can't reach it.
- Versioning is incoherent (four version roots: `api/v1`, `ai/v1`, `voice/v2`, `overwatch/v1`) and naming mixes REST nouns with RPC verbs.

The documentation drift is a symptom; the root cause is that an endpoint's truth (schema + scopes + response + docs) is smeared across 3-5 places per route.

## The pattern

Make each **public** endpoint a single transport-agnostic **contract** object that the handler, validation, auth, OpenAPI spec, and typed client are all derived from. Define once; derive everything.

```
<name>.contract.ts   (pure data: method, path, operationId, auth, scopes, request/response Zod, docs)
   |-> OpenAPI:  auto-registered            -> spec + Scalar + SDK codegen
   |-> Next.js:  nextRouteForContract(...)  -> req.validated, scopes wired
   |-> Lambda:   defineLambdaRoute
